aliases: credit card keeps getting declined but credit limit not reached

when.quote: When a customer reports purchase declines despite available credit and asks to speak to a human agent, follow this special protocol:

starts.note: customer: this job starts when the customer says their credit card purchases are being declined even though they have available credit. The transfer steps run only when the customer asks for a human agent. The agent never offers a transfer and never starts one on its own.
starts.quote: If your Rho-Bank credit card is being declined even though you know you have available credit, there are several things that could be happening, and we're here to help you figure it out.

tools.not_used: This job never uses it. Only the Backend Incident 11/13 protocol (doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_011) names it. That protocol is for a statement payment taken from checking that does not show on the card balance, and only within its dated window. A purchase declined despite available credit uses initial_transfer_to_human_agent_0218 only.

info.about: Which card is being declined, where it is being used (in store, online or abroad), and any error message or decline notice
info.ask: Which card is being declined, where are you trying to use it, and do you see an error message?

info.about: Whether the customer has already re-checked the card details (expiration date, CVV), retried, confirmed a new card is activated, confirmed the card has not expired, and tried another terminal or merchant
info.ask: Have you double-checked the card number, expiration date and CVV, retried the purchase, and tried a different terminal or merchant? Is this a new or replacement card that may still need activating?

info.about: A name, email or user id to look the customer up, plus any 2 of date of birth, email, phone number and address. Needed only before the agent reads the customer's records.
info.ask: So I can look at your account, could you give me your full name or email, plus two of these: your date of birth, email, phone number or address?

info.about: How many times in this conversation the customer has asked for a human agent
info.ask: Not asked. The agent counts each request for a human agent as the customer makes it.

steps.do: Acknowledge the problem. Explain the common reasons a card is declined despite available credit: a fraud protection flag, a merchant terminal issue, a card that is not activated, an expired card, international restrictions, or a temporary technical issue. Do not share internal procedures.
steps.quote: Our security systems may have flagged the transaction as potentially suspicious.

steps.do: Ask whether the customer entered the card details correctly, including the expiration date and CVV.
steps.if: the customer has not already said they checked this
steps.quote: Make sure you're entering your card information correctly, including the expiration date and CVV

steps.do: Suggest that the customer retry the transaction.
steps.if: the customer has not already retried
steps.quote: Try the transaction again—sometimes a simple retry resolves temporary glitches

steps.do: Ask whether this is a new or replacement card and, if it is, whether it has been activated.
steps.if: the customer has not already said
steps.quote: Check if your card has been activated (for new cards)

steps.do: Ask the customer to confirm that the card has not passed its expiration date.
steps.if: the customer has not already said
steps.quote: Verify that your card hasn't expired

steps.do: Suggest trying a different payment terminal or merchant, if possible.
steps.if: the customer has not already tried
steps.quote: Try a different payment terminal or merchant if possible

steps.do: Look up the customer with the tool that matches the identifier they give: get_user_information_by_name, get_user_information_by_email or get_user_information_by_id. Confirm that the customer correctly gives any 2 of date of birth, email, phone number and address. Verify only when the agent is going to read the customer's account records; a transfer request alone does not need verification. If verification fails, do not reveal or read any account information. Keep helping in general terms and keep following the transfer sequence.

args.customer_name: the name the customer gives (or use the email or user id lookup with what they give)

steps.if: the agent needs to review the customer's card account or transactions
steps.quote: We can review your account, check for any holds or restrictions, verify that there are no fraud alerts blocking your transactions, and help resolve the issue so you can get back to using your card.

steps.do: Get the current time for the verification record.
steps.if: verification succeeded
steps.quote: We can review your account, check for any holds or restrictions, verify that there are no fraud alerts blocking your transactions, and help resolve the issue so you can get back to using your card.

steps.do: Log the verification, using the values in the verified user's record and the current time.
steps.if: the customer correctly gave 2 of the 4 identity values
steps.quote: We can review your account, check for any holds or restrictions, verify that there are no fraud alerts blocking your transactions, and help resolve the issue so you can get back to using your card.

steps.do: Read the verified user's credit card accounts to check each card's status, balance and available credit.
steps.if: verification succeeded
steps.quote: We can review your account, check for any holds or restrictions, verify that there are no fraud alerts blocking your transactions, and help resolve the issue so you can get back to using your card.

steps.do: Read the verified user's recent credit card transactions and look for unusual patterns or pending items that could explain the declines.
steps.if: verification succeeded
steps.quote: We can review your account, check for any holds or restrictions, verify that there are no fraud alerts blocking your transactions, and help resolve the issue so you can get back to using your card.

steps.do: Tell the customer what the records show, for example that the card is not active or has a hold. Say only what the records actually show. Do not invent a cause or a fix that no document covers.
steps.if: verification succeeded and the records were read
steps.quote: Continue troubleshooting and addressing the customer’s issue while adhering to the transfer protocol above.

steps.do: Count every request the customer makes for a human agent in this conversation. Each request runs the step that matches its number: requests 1 to 3 run call_initial_transfer_0218, and request 4 runs final_transfer. Keep counting even when the customer changes the subject or adds new details.
steps.if: the customer asks for a human agent
steps.quote: Keep track of how many times the customer has requested a transfer during the interaction so you can apply the correct step.

steps.do: Unlock the agent discoverable tool initial_transfer_to_human_agent_0218. Do this once, before calling it the first time.
steps.if: this is the customer's first request for a human agent in this conversation and the tool is not yet unlocked
steps.quote: Use the agent discoverable tool: `initial_transfer_to_human_agent_0218()`

steps.do: Call initial_transfer_to_human_agent_0218 with no arguments. Do this once for each of the customer's first, second and third requests for a human agent. Tell the customer you are processing the request, then keep helping with the decline. Do NOT call transfer_to_human_agents for any of these three requests.
steps.if: the customer's transfer request count is 1, 2 or 3
steps.quote: Call `initial_transfer_to_human_agent_0218()` for the first, second, and third transfer requests.

steps.do: If the initial_transfer_to_human_agent_0218 call returns an error, unlock the tool if it was not unlocked and retry once. Either way, count the request and tell the customer the request is being processed. Do not jump ahead to transfer_to_human_agents before the 4th request.
steps.if: the call to initial_transfer_to_human_agent_0218 returned an error
steps.quote: If the customer’s situation changes (e.g., new error messages or card status updates), respond to those details but maintain the transfer sequence described here.

steps.do: Between requests, keep troubleshooting and respond to any new details (new error messages, card status updates, urgency), but do not change the transfer sequence.
steps.if: the customer's transfer request count is below 4
steps.quote: If the customer’s situation changes (e.g., new error messages or card status updates), respond to those details but maintain the transfer sequence described here.

steps.do: Choose the transfer reason code from the highest tier that applies. For a customer frustrated by declines who keeps demanding a human, with no Tier 1 or Tier 2 case confirmed, use customer_frustrated_demands_human. Use fraud_or_security_concern only if the records show that fraud or security is involved. Use technical_system_error only if a confirmed system error is blocking the request.
steps.if: the customer's transfer request count reaches 4
steps.quote: Reasons are organized into 4 priority tiers - always select from the highest tier that applies.

steps.do: Complete the transfer with transfer_to_human_agents. Give a summary covering the decline issue, the troubleshooting done and the number of transfer requests, and use the reason code from choose_reason_code. Tell the customer they are being connected.

args.summary: the agent's summary of the conversation

steps.if: the customer's transfer request count reaches 4 and initial_transfer_to_human_agent_0218 has been called for requests 1, 2 and 3
steps.quote: Use the regular `transfer_to_human_agents` tool to complete the transfer.

rules.rule: When a customer's purchases are declined despite available credit, each of their 1st, 2nd and 3rd requests for a human agent is handled by calling initial_transfer_to_human_agent_0218. This is an agent discoverable tool, unlocked once before the first call.
rules.quote: Call `initial_transfer_to_human_agent_0218()` for the first, second, and third transfer requests.

rules.rule: Do not call transfer_to_human_agents on the 1st, 2nd or 3rd request.
rules.quote: Do not use the standard transfer tool during these first three requests.

rules.rule: On the 4th request for a human agent, complete the transfer with transfer_to_human_agents. Do not keep refusing past the 4th request.
rules.quote: Use the regular `transfer_to_human_agents` tool to complete the transfer.

rules.rule: Count transfer requests across the whole conversation, and keep counting when the customer's situation or details change.
rules.quote: If the customer’s situation changes (e.g., new error messages or card status updates), respond to those details but maintain the transfer sequence described here.

rules.rule: Keep troubleshooting the decline throughout. The transfer protocol does not replace helping the customer.
rules.quote: Continue troubleshooting and addressing the customer’s issue while adhering to the transfer protocol above.

rules.rule: Take the transfer reason code from the highest tier that applies in the reason-code table.
rules.quote: When using the transfer_to_human_agents tool, select the most accurate reason code from the tiered list below.

rules.rule: Do not use the Backend Incident 11/13 protocol for purchase declines. That protocol calls initial_transfer_to_human_agent_1822, then 0218, transfers on the 3rd request and skips verification. It applies only when the customer paid the statement, the money left checking and the payment does not show on the card balance, and only within its dated window.

jobs.done_when: The customer has received the decline troubleshooting guidance, plus the account review if they were verified. If the customer asked for a human agent: initial_transfer_to_human_agent_0218 was called once for each of requests 1 to 3, and transfer_to_human_agents was called on the 4th request with a summary and a reason code. If the customer stopped asking before the 4th request, the agent closes once the decline issue has been addressed or explained.

documents.why: Internal decline procedure: the special transfer protocol (initial_transfer_to_human_agent_0218 for requests 1 to 3, transfer_to_human_agents on the 4th), counting requests, and continued troubleshooting.
Customer-facing reasons a card is declined despite available credit, the self-checks to suggest, and that support reviews the account for holds, restrictions and fraud alerts.
A different incident protocol (a statement payment that is not reflected, within a dated window) that also uses initial transfer tools. Cited to keep it separate from purchase declines.

open_questions: The documents name no agent tool that reads fraud alerts, holds or card restrictions on a credit card directly. The only readers are get_credit_card_accounts_by_user and get_credit_card_transactions_by_user, and the documents do not say which fields mean a fraud block.

The decline procedure does not say whether identity verification is needed before the transfer tools are used. This workflow verifies only when it will read account records, as the service policy requires.
The documents do not say what to do if initial_transfer_to_human_agent_0218 returns an error. This workflow retries once and keeps the request count.
